newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha little changed, contango wider.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha little changed, contango wider.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were barely changed in subdued afternoon trade on Tuesday, while the contango in near-term spreads widened amid sluggish buying interest for prompt cargoes, traders said.
The one-month spread from second-half July was discussed at minus $2.00/minus $1.25, compared with late Monday's levels of minus $1.50/minus 50 cents.

The contango, which tightened last week in anticipation of recovering end-user demand for near-term cargoes, started widening again as actual buying interest from petrochemical firms has failed to meet expectations, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half July stood at $214.50/215.50 per tonne. It was traded once at $214.50 and again at $215.40 on Monday.
In term talks, three Japanese trading houses, one Japanese oil firm and one South Korean petrochemical firm, are due to submit their bids for Abu Dhabi term cargoes by Wednesday.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) has already notified buyers of its offer price of $22.50 per tonne over the ADNOC formula for one-year term contracts starting in July.
